item.title: Papercut 0.9.3
item.description:
The call's buttons are in a bar of their own above the picture, as in Google Meet: microphone, camera, share and leave in the middle, the layouts and the chat on the right, and whether you're recording on the left. The same in the browser.

The window has no title bar any more: the pages go up to the top. Settings is the gear beside Session.

Markers and the 1-4 segment keys are gone.

item.title: Papercut 0.9.2
item.description:
Guests in a browser can share their screen, a window or a tab with the call.

Editing: jumping around and dragging on the timeline is fast again in recordings with a shared screen.

Processing and Editing say they're looking for recordings while the app starts, instead of saying there are none.

item.title: Papercut 0.9.1
item.description:
Choosing a sound output in the call works: before, the call kept playing through the Mac's default output.

Choosing a microphone for the call works too: before, a microphone other than the Mac's default could leave the call silent.

Device lists are sorted by name and say which devices are built in, virtual or an iPhone. With two Studio Displays, their cameras, microphones and speakers say left or right.

A MacBook's own camera and microphone aren't offered while its lid is closed: they would only give black and silence.

item.title: Papercut 0.9.0
item.description:
A join screen before the call: your picture with microphone and camera switches, your devices, and who is in the call. Leave goes back to it.

Mute now silences your recording too: nothing said while muted is in any file. Your level meter still works while muted.

Camera off: switch your camera off altogether; the others see your initials.

Everyone's app version shows next to their name, orange when it's older.

Chat: images (drop or paste them), and whoever comes in later sees what was said before.

In the call while the room records means you're recorded: no more Join recording button.

Screen sharing without permission explains where to allow it.

Editing: each speaker's volume, noise gate and colour, and times of day in the list.

Fixes: a black or half-size preview, the window jumping between screens at launch, AirPods' input volume shown as not adjustable.

item.title: Papercut 0.8.0
item.description:
Audio only from a browser: someone without a Mac takes part from a web page (Chrome, Edge, or Safari on an iPad), recorded and sent to the hosts like a Mac, and transcribed on each Mac by itself.

Mute silences your call for real; the others see you muted and no level from you. Nobody sees a level before they join, or before they joined themselves.

Clearer name tags: a red microphone when muted, no name chips over the picture. Session says plainly who is muted or hasn't joined.

While sharing, the floating call can be closed (✕) and taken out again, starts in the same corner as on the stage, and can't get too small.

Chat: web addresses are links, with the pointing hand.

The same person in two places: the newest takes over, unless the other is recording.

Upload speed limit: Adaptive by default, or 2 to 50 Mbit/s.

item.title: Papercut 0.7.0
item.description:
Join and Leave: the call no longer starts by itself. Check yourself in your own picture, then press Join (⌘J). Leave takes you out; during a recording it asks first and stops only your recording. Files keep moving either way.

Chat with the room, saved with the recording.

Screen sharing: sharp and whole, shown in its own shape, large for everyone. While you show another app, the call floats over it, never shared nor recorded. Recorded only during a recording, and listed on the Processing page.

A calmer level meter that tells you whether you're too quiet, good or too loud. Grey while you're muted.

Transfers take turns, show each file's speed, can be cancelled, and the Tasks page shows the totals. The Mac stays awake while files move.

A long microphone gap no longer crashes the app, and transcripts are finished after a crash. Problems nothing can fix can be acknowledged.

Windows come back where you left them. "Listener" is now "audio only".

item.title: Papercut 0.6.0
item.description: <p>Editing: a shared screen shows with the hosts stacked beside it, and on the timeline, in the transcript and in the list. Click the picture to play or pause; jumps and scrubbing are instant and clean.</p><p>In the call, pick which display to share, and see your own shared screen in a tile. Screen recordings keep their true colors.</p><p>Transcripts start a new line after a pause over 2 seconds, and a made-up “TV Gelderland” line is left out. Transcribe Again… on the Processing page brings older recordings up to date.</p><p>Jargon, the words WhisperX should spell your way, is one list for every Mac: Settings → Transcription → Jargon.</p>

item.title: Papercut 0.5.0
item.description:
Recordings go straight between the Macs during the call, replacing the shared folder. Everyone in the room needs this version.

Listeners are recorded by sound (their microphone, never their camera) and combined with the hosts.

Everyone has a three-letter ID and a full name: pick yours in Settings → You.

A Tasks page (⌘4) shows what runs in the background; quitting waits for what would be lost.

Editing: paste the lines a language model kept into the Edit box, and Make Edit… cuts them into a video. The player shows the time of day.

The call keeps itself alive, and the Audio section sets input and output with their volumes.

item.title: Papercut 0.4.0
item.description:
Updates itself from now on: Papercut checks once a day, or right away with Papercut → Check for Updates…

Screen sharing in the call, recorded locally and placed in the combined file.

Listeners, the assistant (OpenRouter too), and Export text on the Processing page.
